abstract: Homologous recombination requires tightly controlled assembly and maturation of RAD51 nucleoprotein filament, yet the mechanistic roles of the RAD51 paralogs remain poorly understood. Here, we show that the human RAD51 paralog complex RAD51C-XRCC3 (CX3) remodels oligomeric RAD51 and promotes filament assembly while capping the 5' filament end to stabilise it. CX3 protects RAD51 filaments from dissociation induced by competitor DNA or BRCA2-derived BRC repeats and converts them into a nuclease-sensitive remodelled state. This transition requires ATP-bound RAD51 and ATP hydrolysis by RAD51C, without altering RAD51 ATPase activity. ATP-binding-defective RAD51 fail to undergo remodeling and instead trigger a futile CX3 ATP turnover, suggesting coupling between RAD51 conformation and CX3 activity. Together, our findings establish CX3 as an ATP-dependent RAD51 filament assembly and remodelling factor and define a mechanism of filament maturation distinct from BRCA2- and BCDX2-mediated RAD51 regulation.

summary: Human RAD51C-XRCC3 complex assembles, caps and stabilises RAD51 filaments, remodelling them via ATP-dependent steps in homologous recombination.
